procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires the factory to be registered (outside a free zone, with a MoIAT industrial licence and a letter confirming 40% domestic value added) before applying for a certificate of origin. Registration takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade issues the certificate through its e-service: log in to the ministry e-services portal, choose the Certificate of Origin for India service, fill in the application form, upload the required documents, pay the fee online, submit the application, and print the approved certificate. Processing takes about one working day and the service runs 24/7.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 50 for an invoice value up to AED 100000.

The competent authority issues the certificate, which is valid for 12 months from issue and covers one import. It must be issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export, and can be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 of India's certificate form.

The exporter must ensure the goods are shipped directly from the UAE to India. Transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. If a third party issues the invoice, the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, holds origin information under CAROTAR 2020, and keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing. The importer must answer a customs request within 10 working days.
The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the calendar year of issue.

caveats.note: The '+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Indian inputs count as originating only with proof of their originating status (bilateral cumulation, Art. 3.7).
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
The duty estimate is on the shipment value given; India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value, so actual amounts will differ.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only; IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The certificate fee is based on the invoice value in AED; it assumes the certificate's invoice value equals the shipment value given.

'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement; the agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating; the last production process in the UAE must still go beyond minimal operations.
The agreement says box 8 for the retrospective mark, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year record-keeping minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate; confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources, not the official text.
